requirements.title: Policy document validation and normal form
requirements.rationale: A policy that is stored must be one the evaluator can apply, and a refused one must tell its author which rule and member to fix.

criteria.condition: a document that satisfies every rule of the format is validated, with any of default, rules, exclude, targets, approvals, approvers, checks, fresh_checks and block left out and with members the format does not define present
criteria.action: accept the document and produce its normal form: default present, every requirement carrying approvals (0 when absent), approvers (['owner'] when absent), checks ([] when absent), fresh_checks (false when absent) and block (false when absent), every rule carrying exclude ([] when absent), targets present only where it was given, rules in the order given, and undefined members removed
criteria.contract: validation returns no error and the normal form; validating the normal form again returns the same normal form

setup: a user lookup stub that knows the username 'dana'
check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/document_test.go, a table over {the empty object {}; the three-rule example of the source PRD (docs, billing with targets and approvers, secrets with block); a rule with only name, paths and require {}; a document with an extra top-level member 'comment' and an extra rule member 'owner_team'; a rule with approvals 10 and a name of 63 characters; a path glob of 255 characters}: nf, err = Validate(raw, users); assert err == nil; assert nf equals the expected normal form of the row (for {}: default {approvals 0, approvers ['owner'], checks [], fresh_checks false, block false} and rules []); assert Validate(marshal(nf), users) returns nf again

criteria.condition: a rule has no name, a name that is not a string, a name that does not match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}$, the name 'default', or a name an earlier rule of the document already has
criteria.action: refuse the document and name the rule and the member
criteria.contract: validation returns the invalid-policy error carrying rule (the rule's name when it is a string, else null), index (the rule's zero-based position) and field 'name'; no normal form is returned

setup: a user lookup stub that knows the username 'dana'
check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/document_test.go, one table of invalid documents, each row {document, want rule, want index, want field}, shared by the name, glob and requirement violations. Name rows: rule without name -> (null, 0, 'name'); name 7 -> (null, 0, 'name'); name 'Docs' -> ('Docs', 0, 'name'); name of 64 characters; name '-x'; name 'default' -> ('default', 0, 'name'); two rules named 'docs' -> ('docs', 1, 'name'). Glob rows: no paths -> field 'paths'; paths [] -> 'paths'; paths ['ok', ''] -> 'paths[1]'; paths ['/abs'] -> 'paths[0]'; a path glob of 256 characters; paths 'docs/**' (a string, not a list) -> 'paths'; exclude ['/x'] -> 'exclude[0]'; targets [] -> 'targets'; targets ['a b'], ['a..b'], ['x.lock'], ['-x'], ['a?'] -> 'targets[0]'. Requirement rows, each once inside a rule (field prefixed 'require.') and once in default (rule 'default', index null, field without prefix): rule without require -> 'require'; approvals -1, 11, 1.5, '1' -> 'approvals'; approvers [] -> 'approvers'; approvers ['team:x'], ['user:'], [3] -> 'approvers[0]'; checks ['Test'], [''], a name of 64 characters -> 'checks[0]'; checks 'test' -> 'checks'; fresh_checks 'yes' -> 'fresh_checks'; block 1 -> 'block'. Top-level rows: a document that is a JSON list or string and not an object -> (null, null, 'document'); rules as an object -> (null, null, 'rules'); default as a list -> ('default', null, 'default'). For each row: nf, err = Validate(row.document, users); assert nf == nil; assert errors.As(err, the invalid-policy error) and its rule, index and field equal the row's

criteria.condition: a rule has no paths, an empty paths list, a paths or exclude entry that is not a string of 1 to 255 characters or that starts with '/', a targets list that is present and empty, or a targets entry that is not a branch glob of 1 to 255 characters (a valid branch name in which * and ** may also appear)
criteria.action: refuse the document and name the rule and the member, with the position of the entry in square brackets when one entry is at fault
criteria.contract: validation returns the invalid-policy error carrying the rule's name, its index and field 'paths', 'paths[i]', 'exclude[i]', 'targets' or 'targets[i]'; no normal form is returned

criteria.condition: the document is not a JSON object, rules is not a list, default is not an object, a rule has no require object, or a requirement (a rule's require, or default) has approvals that is not an integer from 0 to 10, an approvers list that is present and empty, an approvers entry that is not 'owner', 'member' or 'user:' followed by at least one character, a checks entry that does not match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,62}$, or a member of another JSON type than the format gives it
criteria.action: refuse the document and name the rule and the member
criteria.contract: validation returns the invalid-policy error carrying rule (the rule's name, or 'default' with index null, or null for the document as a whole) and field: 'document' for a text that is not an object, 'rules' or 'default' for a top-level member of the wrong type, 'require' for a missing require, otherwise the member name, prefixed 'require.' inside a rule, with the entry's position in square brackets when one entry is at fault; no normal form is returned

criteria.condition: an approvers entry 'user:<username>' names a username for which no user exists when the document is validated
criteria.action: refuse the document and name the rule and the entry
criteria.contract: validation returns the invalid-policy error with field 'require.approvers[i]' (or 'approvers[i]' with rule 'default'); a document naming an existing user of any status is accepted; a failure of the user lookup itself is returned as that failure and not as an invalid-policy error

setup: a user lookup stub that knows 'dana' (active) and 'blocked-bob' (blocked) and no 'nobody'
check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/document_test.go: Validate(rule 'billing' with approvers ['owner','user:nobody']) -> invalid-policy error (rule 'billing', index 0, field 'require.approvers[1]'); default with approvers ['user:nobody'] -> ('default', null, 'approvers[0]'); approvers ['user:dana'] and ['user:blocked-bob'] -> accepted; with a lookup stub that returns an I/O error: err is that error and errors.As(err, invalid-policy) is false

criteria.condition: the document has more than 200 rules, or its JSON text as sent is longer than 65 536 bytes
criteria.action: refuse the document
criteria.contract: validation returns the invalid-policy error with rule null, index null and field 'rules' for the rule count and field 'document' for the size; a document of exactly 200 rules and a text of exactly 65 536 bytes are accepted

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/document_test.go: gen(n) builds n rules named r0..r(n-1) with paths ['a/**'] and require {}; Validate(gen(200)) -> accepted with 200 rules; Validate(gen(201)) -> invalid-policy (null, null, 'rules'); pad a valid one-rule document with white space to exactly 65 536 bytes -> accepted; to 65 537 bytes -> invalid-policy (null, null, 'document'); a 65 537-byte text that also has 201 rules -> field 'document'

criteria.condition: a document breaks more than one rule of the format
criteria.action: report only the first violation, in this order: size, top-level member types, rule count, default, then the rules in document order, and within a requirement or rule the members in the order approvals, approvers, checks, fresh_checks, block and name, paths, exclude, targets, require
criteria.contract: the invalid-policy error names the earliest violation in that order; the same document always yields the same rule, index and field

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/document_test.go, a table: default.approvals 11 and rule 0 name 'X' -> ('default', null, 'approvals'); rule 0 with paths [] and rule 1 with name 'X' -> (rule 0's name, 0, 'paths'); rule 0 with name 'X' and paths [] -> ('X', 0, 'name'); rule 0 with exclude ['/a'] and require.approvals 11 -> field 'exclude[0]'; default with checks ['A'] and approvers [] -> field 'approvers'. Run each row 20 times and assert the same triple every time

requirements.title: Reading the policy
requirements.rationale: People and agents need to see the rules that govern a workspace, and earlier revisions to understand a land that was judged by one.

criteria.condition: a caller with changes:read and read access sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/policy for a workspace whose policy was never set
criteria.action: answer with the revision-0 document
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {revision: 0, default: {approvals: 0, approvers: ['owner'], checks: [], fresh_checks: false, block: false}, rules: [], updated_at: null, updated_by: null} and the header ETag: "0"

criteria.condition: the same request is sent for a workspace whose policy was replaced at least once and no revision query parameter is given
criteria.action: answer with the current revision in normal form and who wrote it when
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with body {revision, default, rules, updated_at (RFC 3339 UTC, whole seconds), updated_by: {actor_type, actor_id, username}} and the header ETag: "<revision>"; updated_by has actor_type 'admin_token' and username null for a revision the admin token wrote

criteria.action: answer with that revision as it was written
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with that revision's document, its updated_at and updated_by, and ETag: "<n>"

requirements.title: Replacing the policy
requirements.rationale: The owner changes the rules with one call, and a concurrent editor must not silently overwrite another's edit.

criteria.condition: the workspace's owner, or the admin token, sends PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/policy with a valid document and either no If-Match header or an If-Match header whose value, bare or in double quotes, equals the stored revision
criteria.action: store the document's normal form as revision stored + 1 and answer with it
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the body and ETag header that GET returns for the new revision; revision is exactly the previous revision plus 1; a following GET returns the same body

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/handlers_test.go: r1 = put(policy, danaKey, example); assert r1.status == 200 and r1.json.revision == 1 and r1.header('ETag') == '"1"' and r1.json.rules[0].require.approvers == ['owner'] (normal form); assert get(policy).json == r1.json; r2 = put(policy, danaKey, example2, header If-Match: 1); assert r2.json.revision == 2; r3 = put(policy, adminToken, example, header If-Match: "2"); assert r3.json.revision == 3; also on workspaces in status pending, cloning and failed: put answers 200

criteria.condition: a replacement is stored
criteria.action: record exactly one parley.policy.update event in the transaction that stores the revision
criteria.contract: one event with type parley.policy.update, workspace the slug, resource_type 'policy', resource_id the slug, action 'update', the caller as actor and metadata {revision: <new revision>, rules: <number of rules>}

criteria.condition: the request carries an If-Match header whose revision differs from the stored revision
criteria.action: refuse the replacement and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 412 with error_type revision_mismatch; the stored revision, its document and the number of parley.policy.update events are unchanged

On a never-set workspace: If-Match: 0 -> 200 with revision 1

criteria.condition: the body is not a JSON object, the document is invalid, or the If-Match value is not a non-negative integer bare or in double quotes
criteria.action: refuse the replacement and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_policy and error.details {rule, index, field} for an invalid document; HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request for a body that is not a JSON object and for a malformed If-Match; the stored revision and the event log are unchanged

requirements.title: Selecting a rule for each touched file
requirements.rationale: Which rule governs a file must be predictable from the document alone: first match in order, by target branch and path.

criteria.action: for any path glob and repository-relative path, report a match only when the glob matches the whole path, where * matches any run of characters, possibly empty, without '/', ** matches any run, possibly empty, including '/', ? matches exactly one character other than '/', and every other character matches itself

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/glob_test.go, a table {glob, path, want}: ('docs/**','docs/a/b.md',true); ('docs/**','docs/',true); ('docs/**','docs',false); ('docs/**','xdocs/a',false); ('*.md','README.md',true); ('*.md','docs/a.md',false); ('**/*.md','docs/a.md',true); ('**/*.md','a/b/c.md',true); ('**/*.md','README.md',false); ('src/*.go','src/.go',true); ('src/*.go','src/a/b.go',false); ('a?c','abc',true); ('a?c','ac',false); ('a?c','a/c',false); ('a?c','abbc',false); ('billing/**','billing/x',true); ('Billing/**','billing/x',false); ('a[b]','a[b]',true); ('a[b]','ab',false); ('a***b','a/x/b',true); ('**','any/path',true); ('exact/file.txt','exact/file.txt',true); ('exact/file.txt','exact/file.txt2',false): assert MatchPath(glob, path) == want

criteria.action: for any `targets` entry and target branch name without refs/heads/, take the answer of MatchBranchGlob of package 11 (internal/workspace/branchglob.go): a match only when the glob matches the whole name, with * and ** as for paths and every other character matching itself

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/evaluate_test.go, through the function rule selection uses, which calls the branch-glob matcher of internal/workspace, a table {glob, branch, want}: ('main','main',true); ('main','main2',false); ('release/*','release/1.2',true); ('release/*','release/1/2',false); ('release/**','release/1/2',true); ('*','main',true); ('*','feature/x',false); ('**','feature/x',true); ('rel*','release',true): assert targetMatches([glob], branch) == want

criteria.condition: a file of a change is evaluated against a document for the change's target branch
criteria.action: select the first rule in document order whose targets is absent or has a glob matching the target branch, and whose paths has a glob matching the file, and whose exclude has no glob matching the file, and select default when no rule qualifies
criteria.contract: the selection is that rule's name, or 'default'

check.pseudocode: in internal/policy/evaluate_test.go, with the document [docs: paths ['docs/**','**/*.md'] exclude ['docs/internal/**']; billing: paths ['billing/**'] targets ['main','release/*']; all-billing: paths ['billing/**']; secrets: paths ['deploy/secrets/**']], a table {file, target, want}: ('docs/a.txt','main','docs'); ('billing/README.md','main','docs') (first match wins over billing); ('docs/internal/x.txt','main','default') (excluded, no later rule); ('billing/a.go','main','billing'); ('billing/a.go','release/2','billing'); ('billing/a.go','dev','all-billing') (targets does not match, next rule does); ('src/a.go','main','default'); ('deploy/secrets/k','dev','secrets'): assert Select(doc, target, file) == want; with rules [] every file selects 'default'

criteria.condition: a change whose current version renames a file is evaluated
criteria.action: treat both the old and the new path of the rename as files of the change
criteria.contract: the files read for the change contain both paths, and each selects its own rule

criteria.action: for any change, take as its files exactly the files that differ between the base_sha and the head_sha of its current version, so that a change stacked on another is evaluated for its own commits only and all touched files are used even past the 2 000 the change object lists

execution_paths.title: A developer sets a policy and the open changes follow it

steps.action: runs parley policy set api --file policy.json with a document that lets docs land freely, requires one approval and two checks for billing/** and blocks deploy/secrets/**
reads the file and sends PUT /api/v1/workspaces/api/policy with the document as JSON

authenticates the caller, decides owner access, validates the document, stores it as revision 1, records parley.policy.update and re-evaluates every draft and open change of the workspace in one transaction, then answers 200
prints the stored document with revision 1 and exits 0
reads its open changes with GET /api/v1/workspaces/api/changes/:number
answers each change with its stored landing: ready for the docs change, pending with the billing requirement for the billing change, blocked for the change under deploy/secrets
runs parley policy get api and parley policy get api --revision 1 and reads the same document back

authentication, access rule and binding guard
the policy handlers, validator, evaluator, revision store and re-evaluation of internal/policy
the change records of internal/change over a real git repository
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against stores in t.TempDir()
workspace 'api' owned by dana, backed by a repository made with git init
three open changes of 'api' touching docs/a.md, billing/a.go and deploy/secrets/k
policy.json in t.TempDir() holding the three-rule example of the source PRD
end_state: parley policy set exited 0 and printed a document with revision 1
the event log holds one parley.policy.update for 'api' with metadata revision 1 and rules 3
the three changes read back with landing.status ready, pending and blocked
parley policy get api --revision 1 exited 0 and printed the same document the set command printed

lets the fork-bound token through to the parent's evaluate route, selects a rule for each path on the default branch and answers 200 with policy_revision, status pending and the docs and billing requirements, writing nothing
